extracted.intended_audience: machine learning / NLP researchers studying LLM mathematical reasoning and robustness
extracted.subtask_short: benchmarking LLM math reasoning under perturbations
extracted.subtask_description: Construct and use perturbed versions of hard math problems to evaluate LLMs' true reasoning vs memorization, comparing simple perturbations (which preserve solution patterns) to hard perturbations (which change problem nature so original solutions no longer apply). Report performance drops across models and analyze sources of failure such as blind memorization and effects of in‑context learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perturbation type — Simple vs Hard
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish between simple perturbations that modify problems while preserving the underlying reasoning patterns of the solutions, and hard perturbations that fundamentally change the nature of the problem so that the original solution steps do not apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use both perturbation types to test whether models rely on pattern memorization (simple perturbations may not break memorized procedures) versus true reasoning (hard perturbations should force a changed solution strategy). MATH-P-Simple and MATH-P-Hard are constructed to embody these two classes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benchmark composition and provenance
rubrics_metrics.description: Benchmark instances should be derived from level-5 (hardest) problems in the MATH dataset; MATH-P-Simple and MATH-P-Hard each consist of 279 perturbed math problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selecting the hardest problems increases the chance that perturbations expose fragility; report the source, difficulty level, and exact count (here 279) so comparisons are reproducible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance degradation (accuracy drop) as primary metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure change in model performance between original problems and perturbed variants (e.g., percent drop in accuracy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report absolute and relative drops across models to quantify robustness. Example observed drops: o1-mini (-16.49%) and gemini-2.0-flash-thinking (-12.9%). Compare across a variety of models to characterize sensitivity to perturbations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detection of memorization vs actual reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether a model is truly reasoning or merely memorizing/automatically applying learned problem-solving skills without checking applicability to modified contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design perturbations that would cause a memorized procedure to fail if the model does not check applicability. Analyze failures to identify the 'novel form of memorization' where models blindly apply skills. Use qualitative case studies and error analyses to illustrate this behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of in‑context learning on robustness
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess how providing original (unperturbed) problems as in-context examples influences model behavior on perturbed problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate models both with and without in-context examples and report whether in-context learning amplifies misapplication of procedures (the paper notes amplification when using original problems for in-context learning). This is an important control when interpreting benchmark results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generalization / robustness to structural changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the model's ability to generalize when the structure or nature of a problem changes (i.e., when solution steps used previously are no longer applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hard perturbations should force different reasoning strategies; success indicates better generalization. Use a mix of perturbation types to probe different structural sensitivities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Call for solutions: robustness and reliability as desiderata
rubrics_metrics.description: Beyond measuring failures, establish as a standard that research should develop methods to prevent blind memorization and improve robustness to hard perturbations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benchmark results should motivate method development; papers should propose or evaluate mitigations (e.g., checks for applicability, improved prompting, training/regimes that encourage flexible reasoning) and measure their effect on MATH-P-Hard and similar datasets.
